newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to suspend operation of fast-breeder reactor.
newsitem.headline: Japan to suspend operation of fast-breeder reactor.

text.p: Japan's science agency said on Monday it will suspend operations at a state-run fast-breeder reactor as a penalty for falsifying reports following a 1995 sodium leak accident.

Although the prototype Monju reactor in Tsuruga on the Sea of Japan coast has been shut since the accident, the measure still carries serious symbolic significance as such a suspension has been imposed only once before, a Science and Technology Agency official said.
"This is not the kind of order we issue every day," he said, adding that the agency had not decided yet when the suspension would begin or how long it would last.
The Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC), which operates the reactor, agreed that the suspension was a serious move.
"The order is not likely to have a significant impact on plant operations as the reactor has already been closed, but that does not stop us from taking the penalty solemnly," a PNC spokesman said.
The science agency's action was prompted by a ruling by Tsuruga Summary Court last month fining PNC and two of its officials for falsifying reports about the sodium leak.
The law governing nuclear reactor operators allows the government to suspend reactor operations or revoke their licences when they are convicted of certain charges.
Domestic media have reported that Monju is likely to be suspended for six months.
The only other suspension order in Japan was issued against the Japan Atomic Power Co's Tsuruga plant after the plant failed to react appropriately to a radiation leak in 1981, the official said.

Operations of the Monju fast-breeder reactor, the cornerstone of Japan's ambitious nuclear fuel recycling programme, began in August 1995, but were halted only four months later when the unit leaked up to three tonnes of sodium from its secondary cooling system.
